newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finns say EU grain plan ignores tough climate.
newsitem.headline: Finns say EU grain plan ignores tough climate.

text.p: European Commission plans to cut support for cereal growers overlook the tough economics of farming in a harsh climate, the Finnish government said on Wednesday.
"The Commission's proposal for a decrease in the price of grain is problematic from Finland's point of view," the agriculture ministry said in a statement.

The EU executive on Wednesday proposed that cereals farmers only be compensated for half of a planned 20 percent cut in support prices in 2000, in a move reflecting criticism that they have been heavily over-paid.
"Finland requires that Finland's special conditions, relatively low crop yields and high cost level, be taken into account in the reform," the ministry said.

"Profitability of grain production in Finland is already low, so a price reduction would further weaken production conditions," it said. The proposed price cuts would mean an annual loss of about 370 million markka to grain producers.
Finland, which joined the European Union in 1995, spans the EU's most northerly territory and has long given extra support to farmers working in long, dark winters in sparsely populated areas.

"Finland also considers it important that also in the future support paid by the EU can be augmented with national support," the statement said. Commission proposals for the beef and dairy sectors were "not as problematic", it added. --Helsinki newsroom +3589 6805 0247, e-mail news@reuters.fi
